hard_constraints: Vara Senn is a former Lost Tribe apprentice, not a Sith Lord. Her Force methods are crude: pressure, fear, domination. She is a crowbar, not a scalpel.
The lightsaber clash is short, cramped, and ugly — thrust, redirect, slam in a narrow aisle. Not a grand duel.
Ben recognizes elements of Lost Tribe training in Vara's patterns. This allows a brief Vestara Khai scar-tissue mention, but Vestara is never on-page.
Vara abandons the lightsaber fight when she senses Iressa is still working. She pivots to hostage tactics.
Greyline arrives as a cleanup team: seal exits, wipe cameras, trigger old quarantine protocols. They are not a battlefield unit.
The archive is a decommissioned GAG quarantine archive on Coruscant. Narrow rows of cabinet-style data storage, single emergency strip lighting along the floor.
Ben's restraint is visible as restraint — he has room to escalate and does not take it. This is the lie-challenged phase for Ben.
Iressa is at the terminal finishing data corruption/transmission. Her death occurs in Ch 15, not Ch 14.
Talon reads exit geometry from behind a cabinet row. He is not in the direct fight.
No Force technique is named in narration before the body has felt it. Avoid clinical or scientific framing of the Force.
Use Star Wars vocabulary: datapads, transparisteel, durasteel, comlinks, blasters, turbolifts, etc.
No ABY/BBY dating in narration or dialogue. Characters reference events directly.
No real-world pop culture references, no Wookieepedia-style taxonomy, no out-of-universe authorial framing.
Capitalize 'Human', lowercase 'galaxy', 'Jedi' singular and plural, 'Darth' capitalized before a name.
canon_risks: Vara Senn is a new character not in published Legends. Ensure she does not contradict any established Lost Tribe lore (e.g., she is a former apprentice, not a high-ranking member).
The GAG quarantine archive is a new setting. Ensure it does not conflict with known GAG infrastructure from the Legacy of the Force novels.
Ben's recognition of Lost Tribe combat patterns must be consistent with his canonical experience with Vestara Khai and the Lost Tribe during Fate of the Jedi.
The archive's quarantine protocols being triggered by Greyline should not imply any ongoing GAG authority — GAG was dissolved after the war.
Vara's Force-pressure and manufactured fear should not be confused with the refined Jacen-derived Recognition technique used by Aevyn. Vara is crude.
legends_continuity_notes: The Lost Tribe of Sith was encountered during the Fate of the Jedi arc (44 ABY). They were largely scattered and broken by 47 ABY. Vara Senn as a former apprentice doing mercenary work is plausible.
Vestara Khai is canonically alive and active off-page under the alias 'Savara Raine' per Crucible (45 ABY). Ben's scar-tissue reaction to Lost Tribe patterns is consistent with his history.
The GAG was dissolved in disgrace after the Battle of Shedu Maad (41 ABY). Its archives would be decommissioned and possibly maintained by civilian contractors or GA Justice.
Coruscant in 47 ABY has no Jedi institutional foothold. The Jedi Temple was vacated in 44 ABY. Ben operates without Order resources or political cover.
Standard Legends holocron canon applies: crystalline storage devices imprinted with Force resonance. Not relevant to this scene but good context.
possible_disney_bleed: No Inquisitorius as a post-Imperial organization. Vara is Lost Tribe, not Inquisitorius.
No kyber crystal bleeding mechanic. Vara's lightsaber (if she has one) would use a synthetic crystal per Legends.
No World Between Worlds, no High Republic references, no sequel-trilogy entities.
No Disney-canon Mandalorian conventions. Not relevant to this scene but worth flagging.
No 'Ben' as Ben Solo. Ben is unambiguously Ben Skywalker.
required_context_for_drafter: This is Pinch Point 1. The antagonist shows organized lethality. Restraint is about to cost something.
Ben is in the lie-challenged phase: he sees a Jacen-shaped coercive move that might save Iressa and refuses it. Iressa dies in Ch 15. The cost of restraint is demonstrated here.
Vara is not the main antagonist. She is a warning shot. Aevyn is the true mirror.
The archive is sealed. Every second Ben holds the aisle is a second Iressa has at the terminal. The turning point is Vara sensing Iressa is still working.
Talon's role is to track exits and read the room. He is not in the direct fight but his awareness is critical.
The Vestara Khai mention should be brief — a scar-tissue reflex, not a full emotional beat. Ben knows this style and knows how to counter it more aggressively than he is willing to.
The fight is cramped: cabinet rows narrow, lightsaber cannot be swung freely. Only thrust, redirect, slam. Emergency strip lighting pulses red when quarantine protocol triggers.
Vara smells of armor sealant and something chemical associated with Lost Tribe Force-pressure. The sensation arrives before she speaks.
Iressa's transmission is the two-part dying package: documentary chain plus identity-shaping revelation. She finishes corrupting the enemy copy and transmits before Vara takes her hostage.
Ben's restraint is visible as restraint — he has room to escalate and does not take it. This is the key character beat for Ben in this scene.
allowed_au_divergences: Vara Senn is a new character (former Lost Tribe apprentice, mercenary). Not in published Legends.
The decommissioned GAG quarantine archive is a new setting for this novel.
Greyline Strategic Services is a new organization (Tess's firm).
The archive cleanup operation is original to this novel.
Ben's recognition of Lost Tribe patterns and the Vestara scar-tissue mention are consistent with canon but the specific scene is original.
open_questions: Does Vara Senn have a lightsaber? The scene card implies she engages Ben in a lightsaber clash. If so, what color? (Legends Lost Tribe used various colors, often red or synthetic.)
What specific quarantine protocols does Greyline trigger? Need to ensure they are plausible for a decommissioned GAG archive.
How does Vara sense Iressa is hiding something? Through crude Force-pressure reading? Body language? The scene card says 'reads Iressa's body language' but also implies Force sensitivity.
What is the exact nature of the 'chemical' smell Ben associates with Lost Tribe Force-pressure? This needs to be a sensory detail that does not contradict established lore.
Is Talon armed? He is a former GAG field agent recently escaped from prison. Does he have a blaster or other weapon in this scene?
